subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• John Williams is an American composer known for film scores.
• The media outlet NPR has described his music as 'iconic orchestral compositions that define blockbuster cinema.'
• His acclaimed film scores feature many talented soloists.
• Yo-Yo Ma played cello on his 1997 film score for Seven Years in Tibet.
• Itzhak Perlman played violin on his 1993 film score for Schindler's List.
prompt: The student wants to emphasize a similarity between Yo-Yo Ma and Itzhak Perlman. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Yo-Yo Ma performed on John Williams's first film score, which was released one year before his score for Schindler's List.
choices.B: Seven Years in Tibet and Schindler's List, released in 1997 and 1993, respectively, are films scored by composer John Williams.
choices.C: Although both musicians have performed on John Williams scores, Yo-Yo Ma played cello, whereas Itzhak Perlman played violin.
choices.D: Yo-Yo Ma and Itzhak Perlman both lent their musical talents to film scores by John Williams in the 1990s.

explanation: Choice D is the best answer because it most effectively emphasizes a similarity between the two musicians. By using the word 'both' and naming Yo-Yo Ma and Itzhak Perlman together, the sentence explicitly highlights what they share in common: contributing their musical talents to John Williams film scores in the same decade. This direct identification of their shared characteristic accomplishes the stated goal of emphasizing similarity.
